name: Zillow on AI in Real Estate: Valuation Models, Agent Tools and Leasing Assistants
title: Zillow on AI in Real Estate: Valuation Models, Agent Tools and Leasing Assistants
answer: Zillow's own site documents how it uses machine learning in production, from the Zestimate home valuation model to AI call summaries and leasing assistants. Its most useful disclosure is the Zestimate methodology: a neural network model drawing on public records, MLS feeds and home characteristics, published for more than 120 million homes and updated several times a week. The site also reports measured results from AI tools used by agents and property managers.

sections.body: Zillow publishes this material across its consumer and Pro pages. The Zestimate page is a product explanation of Zillow's automated valuation model. The Pro pages are a guidance article on AI prompts for agents, two case studies, one on agent training and one on rental leasing, and two conference recaps from Unlock 2024 and Unlock 2025. The pages were read on 3 October 2026. The material mixes product documentation with vendor case studies and event reporting, so it is partly promotional.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The Zestimate is Zillow's estimate of a home's market value, produced by a neural network model that incorporates county and tax assessor records, direct MLS feeds, home characteristics such as square footage, location and bedroom and bathroom counts, on-market data such as listing price, description, comparable homes and days on market, and off-market data such as tax assessments and prior sales. The latest model uses an updated neural network architecture and expanded historical data to improve accuracy for both on-market and off-market homes, and most Zestimates update multiple times per week. Elsewhere the site describes AI in agent workflows. A Virginia team used MaverickRE, which works with Follow Up Boss, to let agents practise with AI-powered leads, and the share of intro calls including a request to meet rose from about 25% to almost 70% after a month. Follow Up Boss shipped an AI feature that drafts talking points and email copy from call transcripts in four days rather than the planned 2026 date, and more than 6.2 million messages have been sent with it. Zillow also built and open-sourced a tool to help AI developers abide by fair housing regulations, and listings can be seen in ChatGPT.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Zillow publishes Zestimates for more than 120 million homes and holds data on more than 125 million homes. The Zestimate model is a neural network drawing on assessor records and MLS feeds, and most estimates update multiple times per week. Follow Up Boss shipped its transcript-based drafting feature in four days instead of 2026, with over 6.2 million messages sent. A Virginia team of 80 agents saw meeting requests on intro calls rise from about 25% to almost 70% after a month of AI role-play. Scully Company, with 42 communities, reported lead-to-tour conversion of 23% from February to May 2026, up from 18% a year earlier, and Zillow-generated leads at one property rising from 33 to 90. Zillow's 2024 call summarisation feature generated more than 5 million summaries in its first week, and a small percentage were fabricated when calls captured butt dials or missing audio.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: This is one of the few places where a major portal describes its production machine learning in public. The Zestimate page gives a reader the model inputs, the architecture and the update cadence behind a consumer-facing automated valuation model, which is useful for anyone assessing how AVMs are built and how often they change. The case studies supply measured outcomes rather than claims, covering agent training, lead conversion and after-hours leasing coverage, and the 2024 recap is candid that summarisation AI invented content when audio was poor. Together they show where AI is already embedded in listing, valuation and leasing workflows.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: The Zestimate page does not publish error rates or accuracy statistics, so the methodology is described without performance figures. The Pro articles and case studies are marketing material for Zillow products and partners, and the results come from single teams and properties rather than controlled studies. The conference recaps are event summaries. Nothing here covers competing valuation models or independent evaluation of the Zestimate.
